newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble eases, no impact seen from rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Rouble eases, no impact seen from rate cut.

text.p: The rouble eased on Friday on client selling and dealers said the market, strictly controlled by the central bank, was unaffected by a refinancing rate cut.
The central bank said on Friday it is cutting its refinancing rate to 48 from 60 percent from December 2.
roubles/dollar Nov 29 midday Nov 29 early Nov 28 close
NOTE - No deals for today settlement were struck on Thursday due to the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday. Russian banks use U.S. banks for settlement.

"The rate cut had no impact on the rouble/dollar market because it is ruled by strict, and effective, central bank's measures and depends on bank client dollar demand," ABN-Amro Bank chief dealer Dmitry Piskulov said.
"It could otherwise be a becalming factor in the longer term implying the inflation will not be high and financial stabilisation is the aim," he added.
Neftekhimbank dealer Boris Golub said roubles were cheap ahead of the week-end, with banks fulfilling client orders to buy dollars.
